failure_progression.judgment: The negedge-reset plus deterministic zero initialization changed the failure class: M2063 crossed preload and executed to the selected ordinary completion boundary. It did not establish mapped equivalence because the completion ledger then disagreed with the frozen source-RTL identity.

future_post_deadline_diagnostic_only_dir: Start from a new non-power development namespace, not a fourth M2063-style one-shot.
Emit each of the ten actual and expected completion fields and identify the first divergent cycle with an RTL-versus-mapped differential trace.

next_step_decision.reason: Three successively improved no-retry attempts have consumed the ISCAS power branch without a mapped functional pass or one SAIF. Another power runner would repeat evidence acquisition before locating the completion divergence.

p1_findings: P1-1: failure.json labels the failure as runtime fatal/XZ, but mapped_sim.log contains no mapped-X/Z fatal. The observed failure is the line-275 completion-ledger aggregate fatal. Future summaries must not repeat the X/Z classification.
p2_findings: P2-1: check_selected_completion folds measured cycles plus nine work/cache/weight ledgers into one fatal and prints no actual values. The failing member, value and first divergence are therefore not uniquely recoverable from the sealed evidence.

P2-2: No waveform, per-counter final dump or cycle-by-cycle RTL/mapped differential trace was captured. The elapsed run and SVA coverage cannot substitute for completion identity or identify whether one or multiple ledger terms drifted.

paper_decision.recommended_action: Keep ISCAS claims at RTL-cycle plus pre-macro logic-area scope and mark measured mapped power unavailable; prioritize the already authorized FC2 continuation evidence and manuscript closure instead of a fourth power attempt.

arithmetic_or_workload_failure.reason: No arithmetic-mismatch, duplicate-commit, protocol, stale or overflow fatal appears before the completion check, and M2057 source RTL passes the same frozen workload. The M2063 wrapper nevertheless stops before the source TB's full final ledger/PASS protocol.

deterministic_init_effect.reason: Unlike M2058 and M2061, M2063 emits no X/Z fatal and reaches the ordinary completion wait after 20,679 SVA attempts. It still fails frozen completion identity.

mapped_completion_counter_identity_drift.reason: The wrapper can leave wait(base_done_cycle >= 0) only after ordinary bundle completion, then line 275 fires because at least one of ten frozen completion comparisons rejects.

mapped_silicon_hardware_defect.reason: The experiment is deterministic-init, zero-delay mapped simulation without SDF or a silicon power-on model. The opaque counter mismatch does not identify a physical defect.

unique_failing_ledger_member.reason: The ten-way condition prints only a generic fatal, and neither the quarantine nor its exactly fingerprinted raw tree contains a waveform or final member values.

runtime_timeline.fatal_text: M2063 ordinary mapped completion ledger drift

verdict: M2063 is a conclusively consumed failure and must never be retried or cited as mapped functionality, SAIF, PTPX, power, or energy evidence. Both its attempt token and failure quarantine are exhaustively double-seal-valid; all 112 raw-work members exactly match the sealed fingerprint, and the three quarantined logs are byte-identical to raw work. This is not another observed X/Z failure: deterministic init allowed the ordinary axis to complete the 383-cycle preload, enter the SAIF window, execute for 20,679 SVA attempts and reach base_done_cycle, after which the ten-way frozen completion check failed at 62,037,010 ps. The exact drifting member cannot be recovered because the checker emits neither member names nor actual values and no waveform exists. The only justified root-cause class is ordinary mapped completion/counter identity drift relative to the M2057 source-RTL ledger; arithmetic failure and silicon defect are not proven. The runner's generic failure.json X/Z label is inaccurate. Given three consumed attempts and zero SAIF/PTPX results, no fourth mapped-power successor is authorized for the ISCAS window.
